name: Kanasi
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 2 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: SIL PNG. n.d. Organised Phonology Data: Kanasi (Sona) Language [SOQ], Rabaraba - Milne Bay Province (Trans New Guinea Phylum; Dagan Family). Data checked by Royers (October 1994), updated Nov 1997, printed August 24, 2004. SIL, Ukarumpa. 4 pp. downloaded via web…
catalog_quote: Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length) There are a number of minimal pairs with stress. However, stress seems to be grammatically conditioned. The second vowel in the verb root is stressed and the second vowel in the noun stem is stressed. tópa 'will chop' íde 'it is burning' topá 'mud' idé 'yes, enough'

audit.reasoning: (1) Deciding quote confirmed verbatim at OPD p.3 in the PDF we hold. (2) The classification rests on a 4-page SIL Organised Phonology Data sheet (Royer & Royer, 1994/1997): primary fieldworker data but a two-sentence, explicitly hedged statement with two minimal pairs and no treatment of affixed forms, secondary stress or exceptions. (3) Against Glottolog 5.1 (2 descriptive refs total) and the SIL archive listing, nothing better is published: Pappenhagen 1986 (held) has no stress rule; Royer & Royer 1990 Grammar essentials (111 pp ms.) and the 1993 Royer phonology 'additional papers' are unpublished Ukarumpa manuscripts, not online (Glottolog's scan of the 1990 ms. is flagged non-shareable). No journal phonology, dissertation or instrumental work on Kanasi was found in Glottolog CLDF

sources.quote: Bibliographic only: both SIL listings show exactly two Kanasi linguistics items — Royer & Royer 1994 Kanasi Organised Phonology Data (online; archive 42441) and Pappenhagen 1986 grammar sketch (archive 40201, 'Not Online' at SIL; we hold the UND copy). No Grammar Essentials or Phonology Essentials ms. was online. Current sil.org / pnglanguages.sil.org pages are behind a an automated-access block (could not be reached by automated download and direct download), so post-2015 additions could not be checked.
